translation_en: Abu al-Tahir, Ahmad ibn Amr ibn Sarh, Harmalah ibn Yahya, and Amr ibn Sawwad al-Amiri narrated to me; their wordings are close. They said: Ibn Wahb narrated to us, saying: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, who said: Urwah ibn al-Zubayr narrated to me that Aishah, the Prophet's wife, told him that she said to the Messenger of Allah: Messenger of Allah, did you ever face a day harder than the day of Uhud? He said: I suffered much at the hands of your people, and the hardest of what I suffered from them was on the day of al-Aqabah, when I presented myself to Ibn Abd Yalil ibn Abd Kulal, but he did not respond to what I wanted. I set out, distressed, facing ahead, and did not come to my senses until I reached Qarn al-Thaalib. I raised my head and saw a cloud shading me. I looked and saw Gabriel in it. He called me and said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has heard what your people said to you and how they answered you. He has sent to you the Angel of the Mountains, so you may command him concerning them as you wish. The Angel of the Mountains called me, greeted me, and said: Muhammad, Allah has heard what your people said to you. I am the Angel of the Mountains, and your Lord has sent me to you so you may command me as you wish. If you wish, I can bring the two mountains upon them. The Messenger of Allah said to him: Rather, I hope that Allah will bring forth from their descendants people who worship Allah alone and associate nothing with Him.

Yahya ibn Yahya and Qutaybah ibn Said narrated to us, both from Abu Awanah. Yahya said: Abu Awanah informed us, from al-Aswad ibn Qays, from Jundub ibn Sufyan, who said: The Messenger of Allah's finger was bloodied in one of those battles, and he said: You are only a finger that has been bloodied; what you have suffered is in the cause of Allah.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated this to us, both from Ibn Uyaynah, from al-Aswad ibn Qays, with this chain of transmission. He said that the Messenger of Allah was in a cave and his finger was injured.

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: Sufyan informed us, from al-Aswad ibn Qays, who heard Jundub say: Gabriel was delayed in coming to the Messenger of Allah, and the polytheists said, 'Muhammad has been abandoned.' Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: 'By the morning brightness, and by the night when it grows still: Your Lord has neither forsaken you nor detested you.' (Quran 93:1-3)

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim and Muhammad ibn Rafi narrated to us; the wording is Ibn Rafi's. Ishaq said: He informed us; Ibn Rafi said: Yahya ibn Adam narrated to us, Zuhayr narrated to us, from al-Aswad ibn Qays, who said: I heard Jundub ibn Sufyan say: The Messenger of Allah was unwell and did not get up for two or three nights. A woman came to him and said: Muhammad, I hope your devil has left you; I have not seen him come near you for two or three nights. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: 'By the morning brightness, and by the night when it grows still: Your Lord has neither forsaken you nor detested you.' (Quran 93:1-3)

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, and Ibn Bashshar narrated to us. They said: Muhammad ibn Jafar narrated to us, from Shubah. [Another chain:] Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: al-Mulai informed us, Sufyan narrated to us. Both chains report it from al-Aswad ibn Qays, with this chain, in wording similar to their hadith.

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Hanzali, Muhammad ibn Rafi, and Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us; the wording is Ibn Rafi's. Ibn Rafi said: He narrated to us; the other two said: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, Mamar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Urwah, that Usamah ibn Zayd told him that the Prophet rode a donkey with a saddle beneath a Fadaki cloak, and seated Usamah behind him. He was visiting Sad ibn Ubadah among Banu al-Harith ibn al-Khazraj, before the Battle of Badr. He passed a gathering containing a mixture of Muslims, polytheists who worshipped idols, and Jews. Abdullah ibn Ubayy was among them, and Abdullah ibn Rawahah was in the gathering. When dust raised by the animal covered the gathering, Abdullah ibn Ubayy covered his nose with his cloak and said: Do not cover us with dust. The Prophet greeted them, stopped, dismounted, invited them to Allah, and recited the Quran to them. Abdullah ibn Ubayy said: Man, there is nothing better than this, if what you say is true. Do not disturb us in our gatherings; return to your riding place, and whoever comes to you from among us, tell him about it. Abdullah ibn Rawahah said: Come to our gatherings, for we like that. The Muslims, polytheists, and Jews began arguing until they nearly attacked one another. The Prophet continued calming them, then rode his animal until he entered upon Sad ibn Ubadah. He said: Sad, did you hear what Abu Hubab (meaning Abdullah ibn Ubayy) said, such-and-such? Sad said: Messenger of Allah, pardon him and overlook it. By Allah, Allah has given you what He has given you. The people of this settlement had agreed to crown him and bind the crown around him, but when Allah turned that aside through the truth He gave you, he was embittered by it. That is why he acted as you saw. The Prophet pardoned him.

Muhammad ibn Rafi narrated to me: Hujayn (meaning Ibn al-Muthanna) narrated to us, Layth narrated to us, from Uqayl, from Ibn Shihab, with a similar report in this chain, adding: This was before Abdullah became Muslim.

Muhammad ibn Abd al-Ala al-Qaysi narrated to us: al-Mutamir narrated to us, from his father, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Prophet was told, 'Would you go to Abdullah ibn Ubayy?' He set out to him, riding a donkey, and the Muslims went with him. The land was marshy. When the Prophet came to him, Abdullah said: Keep away from me! By Allah, your donkey's stench has bothered me. A man from the Ansar said: By Allah, the donkey of the Messenger of Allah smells better than you. A man from Abdullah's people became angry on his behalf, and each man's companions became angry. They began striking one another with palm branches, hands, and sandals. We were told that this verse was revealed about them: 'If two groups of believers fight, make peace between them.' (Quran 49:9)

Ali ibn Hujr al-Sadi informed us: Ismail (meaning Ibn Ulayyah) narrated to us: Sulayman al-Taymi narrated to us: Anas ibn Malik narrated to us, saying: The Messenger of Allah said: Who will find out for us what Abu Jahl has done? Ibn Masud set out and found that the two sons of Afra had struck him until he fell to his knees. Ibn Masud took him by the beard and said: Are you Abu Jahl? He replied: Is there anyone above a man whom you have killed—or, he said, whom his own people have killed? Abu Mujliz said: Abu Jahl said: If only someone other than a farmer had killed me.

Hamid ibn Umar al-Bakrawi narrated to us: Mutamir narrated to us, saying: I heard my father say: Anas narrated to us, saying: The Messenger of Allah said: Who will tell me what Abu Jahl has done? He reported something similar to Ibn Ulayyah's hadith, and Abu Mujliz's statement as Ismail mentioned it.

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Hanzali and Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Miswar al-Zuhri narrated to us, both from Ibn Uyaynah; the wording is al-Zuhri's. Sufyan narrated to us, from Amr, who said: I heard Jabir say: The Messenger of Allah said: Who will deal with Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf? He has harmed Allah and His Messenger. Muhammad ibn Maslamah said: Messenger of Allah, would you like me to kill him? He said: Yes. Muhammad said: Give me permission to say something. He said: Say it. Muhammad went to Ka'b, spoke to him, and said: This man is demanding charity from us and has burdened us. When Ka'b heard this, he said: By Allah, you will become even more fed up with him. Muhammad said: We have followed him now, and we dislike leaving him until we see where his affair leads. I wanted you to lend me a loan. Ka'b asked: What will you give me as security? Muhammad said: Whatever you want. Ka'b said: Give me your women as security. Muhammad replied: You are the most handsome of the Arabs; should we pledge our women to you? Ka'b said: Then pledge your children to me. Muhammad replied: One of our sons would be insulted, and people would say, 'He was pledged for two wasqs of dates.' Instead, we will pledge our armor to you. Ka'b said: Yes. Muhammad promised to come back with al-Harith, Abu Abs ibn Jabr, and Abbad ibn Bishr. They came and called Ka'b at night, and he came down to them. Sufyan said that someone other than Amr reported that Ka'b's wife said to him: I hear a sound like blood dripping. He said: It is only Muhammad ibn Maslamah, his foster brother, and Abu Nailah. A noble man would answer a call to a spear thrust at night. Muhammad said: When Ka'b comes, I will reach for his head; when I have a firm hold of him, then you act. When Ka'b came down, wearing his cloak, they said: We smell perfume on you. He said: Yes, so-and-so is beneath me; she is the most fragrant of Arab women. He asked: Will you let me smell it? Ka'b said: Yes, smell it. Muhammad reached for him and smelled him, then said: May I do so again? Ka'b said: Yes. Muhammad got a firm hold of his head, then said: Now, attack him. They killed him.

The narrator said: Qutaybah ibn Said and Muhammad ibn Abbad narrated to us; the wording is Ibn Abbad's. They said: Hatim (Ibn Ismail) narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Abi Ubayd, the freedman of Salamah ibn al-Akwa, from Salamah ibn al-Akwa, who said: We went with the Messenger of Allah to Khaybar and traveled through the night. One of the people said to Amir ibn al-Akwa: Will you recite some of your verses for us? Amir was a poet, so he dismounted and began urging the people onward with these lines: O Allah, were it not for You, we would not have been guided, given charity, or prayed. Forgive us, may I be sacrificed for You, for what we have followed; make our feet firm when we meet the enemy, and send tranquility down upon us. When we are summoned, we answer, and they rely on our battle cry. The Messenger of Allah asked: Who is that rider? They said: Amir. He said: May Allah have mercy on him. A man said: It is due, Messenger of Allah; if only you had let us benefit from him longer. We reached Khaybar and besieged them until severe hunger struck us. Then he said: Allah has granted you victory over it. In the evening of the day it was conquered, the people lit many fires. The Messenger of Allah asked: What are these fires, and what are you cooking? They said: Meat. He asked: What meat? They said: The meat of domestic donkeys. The Messenger of Allah said: Pour it out and break the pots. A man said: Or should we pour it out and wash the pots? He said: That too. When the people lined up, Amir's sword was short. He struck at a Jew's lower leg, but the sword's edge turned back and hit Amir's knee, and he died from it. When we returned, Salamah was holding my hand. The Messenger of Allah saw me silent and asked: What is wrong? I said: May my father and mother be sacrificed for you, they claim Amir's deeds have been nullified. He asked: Who said that? I said: So-and-so, so-and-so, and Usayd ibn Hudayr al-Ansari. He said: Whoever said that has lied. He has a double reward. He joined his two fingers and said: He strove and fought; few Arabs have walked as he did. Qutaybah differed from Muhammad in two words of the hadith; in Ibn Abbad's narration it says, 'Send tranquility down upon us.'

I was also told by Abu al-Tahir: Ibn Wahb informed us, Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, who said: Abd al-Rahman informed me (others besides Ibn Wahb identified him as Ibn Abd Allah ibn Kab ibn Malik), that Salamah ibn al-Akwa said: On the day of Khaybar, my brother fought fiercely alongside the Messenger of Allah, but his sword turned back on him and killed him. The Companions of the Messenger of Allah discussed this and had doubts about him, since a man had died by his own weapon; they were uncertain about some aspects of his case. Salamah said: When the Messenger of Allah returned from Khaybar, I said: Messenger of Allah, give me permission to recite rajaz poetry for you. He gave him permission. Umar ibn al-Khattab said: I know what you will say. I said: By Allah, were it not for Allah, we would not have been guided, given charity, or prayed. The Messenger of Allah said: You have spoken truly. And send tranquility down upon us, make our feet firm when we meet the enemy, for the polytheists have transgressed against us. When I finished my verses, the Messenger of Allah asked: Who said this? I said: My brother said it. He said: May Allah have mercy on him. I said: Messenger of Allah, some people hesitate to pray over him, saying that a man died by his own weapon. The Messenger of Allah said: He died striving and fighting. Ibn Shihab said: Then I asked a son of Salamah ibn al-Akwa, and he narrated something similar from his father, except that when I said some people hesitate to pray over him, the Messenger of Allah said: They have lied. He died striving and fighting, and he has a double reward. He pointed with his two fingers.

Muhammad ibn Abbad and Qutaybah ibn Said narrated to us: Hatim (Ibn Ismail) narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Abi Ubayd, from Salamah ibn al-Akwa, who said: We went with the Messenger of Allah to Khaybar. Then Allah granted them victory over it. In the evening of the day it was conquered, the people lit many fires. The Messenger of Allah asked: What are these fires, and what are you cooking? They said: Meat. He asked: What kind of meat? They said: Domestic donkey meat. The Messenger of Allah said: Pour it out and break the pots. A man said: Messenger of Allah, should we pour it out and wash the pots? He said: Or that.

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim informed us: Hammad ibn Masadah and Safwan ibn Isa informed us. [Another chain:] Abu Bakr ibn al-Nadr narrated to us: Abu Asim al-Nabil narrated to us. All of them report it from Yazid ibn Abi Ubayd with this chain of transmission.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar narrated to us; the wording is Ibn al-Muthanna's. They said: Muhammad ibn Jafar narrated to us, Shubah narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, who said: I heard al-Bara say: On the day of the Confederates, the Messenger of Allah was carrying earth with us, and the earth covered the whiteness of his abdomen. He was saying: By Allah, were it not for You, we would not have been guided, given charity, or prayed. Send tranquility down upon us, for those people have refused us. He said that sometimes he said: The assembly has refused us; when they want to cause discord, we refuse. He raised his voice while saying it.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us: Shubah narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, who said: I heard al-Bara... Then he mentioned a similar report, except that he said: 'Those people have transgressed against us.'

Abdullah ibn Maslamah al-Qanabi narrated to us: Abd al-Aziz ibn Abi Hazim narrated to us, from his father, from Sahl ibn Sad, who said: The Messenger of Allah came to us while we were digging the Trench and carrying earth on our shoulders. The Messenger of Allah said: O Allah, there is no life except the life of the Hereafter, so forgive the Emigrants and the Helpers.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar narrated to us; the wording is Ibn al-Muthanna's. Muhammad ibn Jafar narrated to us: Shubah narrated to us, from Muawiyah ibn Qurrah, from Anas ibn Malik, from the Prophet, who said: O Allah, there is no life except the life of the Hereafter, so forgive the Helpers and the Emigrants.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar narrated to us. Ibn al-Muthanna said: Muhammad ibn Jafar narrated to us, Shubah informed us, from Qatadah, who said: Anas ibn Malik narrated to us that the Messenger of Allah used to say: O Allah, the life is the life of the Hereafter. Shubah said that he may instead have said: O Allah, there is no life except the life of the Hereafter, so honor the Helpers and the Emigrants.

Yahya ibn Yahya and Shayban ibn Farrukh narrated to us. Yahya said: He informed us; Shayban said: Abd al-Warith narrated to us, from Abu al-Tayyah, who said: Anas ibn Malik narrated to us: They used to recite verses while the Messenger of Allah was with them, saying: O Allah, there is no good except the good of the Hereafter, so grant victory to the Helpers and the Emigrants. In Shayban's narration, it says 'forgive' instead of 'grant victory.'

Muhammad ibn Hatim narrated to me: Bahz narrated to us: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us: Thabit narrated to us, from Anas, that the Companions of Muhammad used to say on the day of the Trench: We are the ones who pledged allegiance to Muhammad to remain upon Islam forever—or he said, to fight jihad. Hammad was uncertain. The Prophet would say: O Allah, the good is the good of the Hereafter, so forgive the Helpers and the Emigrants.

Qutaybah ibn Said narrated to us: Hatim (meaning Ibn Ismail) narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Abi Ubayd, who said: I heard Salamah ibn al-Akwa say: I set out before the first call to prayer. The Messenger of Allah's milch camels were grazing at Dhu Qarad. A boy belonging to Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf met me and said: The Messenger of Allah's milch camels have been taken. I asked: Who took them? He replied: Ghatafan. I cried out three times: To the attack at dawn! My cry was heard throughout the two rocky lava tracts of Madinah. Then I rushed after them until I caught up with them at Dhu Qarad, where they had begun drawing water. I shot arrows at them, for I was an archer, saying: I am the son of al-Akwa, and today is the day of the suckling babes. I kept reciting battle verses until I rescued the camels from them and seized thirty cloaks from them. The Prophet and the people arrived. I said: Prophet of Allah, I have kept the people away from the water, and they are thirsty, so send someone after them now. He said: Ibn al-Akwa, you have prevailed, so be gentle. Then we returned, and the Messenger of Allah seated me behind him on his camel until we entered Madinah.
